text:
The Blackhawks came into this one without a win in six games (0-5-1) and with their coach's job in the headlines; earlier this week Connor Bedard said the team has "100 percent belief" in Jeff Blashill, per NHL.com. For two periods it looked like the slide would reach seven. Then Frank Nazar tied it in the third and Ryan Donato won it 3:12 into overtime, 3-2.

Buffalo was the better team early. Owen Power opened the scoring with a slap shot at 9:00, and after Nazar's power-play goal tied it, Tage Thompson put the Sabres back in front on their own power play at 15:46. The Sabres won the first and second periods on expected goals (the quality of their chances), 0.78 to 0.39 and 0.73 to 0.38, and they out-attempted Chicago 51 to 40 for the night. But they never added a third goal, and that left room.

Chicago owned the third, 1.19 to 0.59 in expected goals, and the tying goal came at 8:22: Nazar tipped one in, with Sam Rinzel and Oliver Moore assisting, and the Hawks' win chance went from 22% to 52%. Nazar had five shots, two goals, and was on the ice for 0.05 expected goals against all night, which is about as clean as a forward's night gets. In overtime Patrick Kane, back after missing three games, had the best look of the extra period, a 31% chance that didn't go in. Donato's winner was assisted by Anton Frondell and Rinzel, his second helper of the night.

Over the whole game it was close to a coin flip, 2.47 expected goals for Chicago to 2.10 for Buffalo, and our replays of every shot give the Hawks this one 57% of the time. Spencer Knight made 21 saves, Alex Lyon 22. Kane's postgame media video was titled "It feels good to win", which after six straight without one sounds about right.

For Buffalo this was another loss after an 8-3 defeat at home to Tampa Bay, and a point in Chicago won't change the mood around a team that, by the numbers, should have put this one away in the second period.
headline: Donato ends Chicago's six-game slide in overtime
